newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end softer, mood bearish.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end softer, mood bearish.

text.p: French shares ended weaker on Friday amid continued bearish sentiment over the French budget and labour outlook and expected poor corporate results.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 6.95 points or 0.35 percent at 1,970.61, and was down nearly 50 points on the week. The CAC-40 futures contract finished unchanged at 1978.0 while the broader SBF-20 index ended 3.81 points lower at 1,396.
"The labour climate is not very good. The franc is weak. The half-year corporate earnings results won't be great. There's not much grounds for optimism for next week," said one dealer.
Volume totalled five billion francs, swollen by block trades linked to the expiry of August options and future contracts.
Shares started in loss, then nudged into positive territory before weakness on Wall Street triggered by another burst of U.S. data showing a stronger economy and raising fears of rate tightening.
A stronger franc, the announcement of a 20,000 fall in July unemployment as well as calls for optimism by President Jacques Chirac failed to lift the market's mood.
"In addition to all our home-grown problems, we've got the worries about rates in the United States," said another dealer.
Ignoring futures-related activity, underlying business was low and foreign investors are steering clear of French assets, another broker said. Domestic investors are taking profits.

* Insurer Axa ended down 3.10 francs at 284.20, after announcing it had completed sale of a 9.7 percent stake in reinsurer Scor, netting 22.5 million francs. AGF finished down 0.5 francs at 131.0 after announcing it sold virtually all of its 9.7 percent stake. It netted 47 million francs.
Scor finished up 2.0 percent at 206.0 francs, continuing its strong run.

The Scor shares were sold into the market and not to trade buyers, which analysts said dampened speculation that it might become a takeover target. Analysts said investors buying the shares were looking for value with one saying he had a year-end share price target of 250 francs.

"I don't see anybody committing to anything. I think it's reasonable to assume that Axa and AGF would have offered their stakes to a trade buyer before going to the market with them," said an analyst.

UAP finished up 0.80 francs at 101.80. It said it would sell a significant part of its 40.9 percent stake if market conditions were ripe when Scor lists in New York, a move expected sometime this autumn.

* Alcatel Alsthom shares ended up 1.2 francs at 392.0. Alcatel and Britain's General Electric Co Plc announced on Friday they would study a possible merger between their joint venture engineering company GEC Alsthom and France's state-controlled nuclear power plant maker Framatome.
